concepts.name: The phone on stone
concepts.headline: Booked online. Confirmed by a call.
concepts.subcopy: Customers book online. Your AI follows up with a confirmation call, and you see the call details in your dashboard.
concepts.cameraMotion: Begin close to the stone surface, rise toward a sculptural phone, then move through its screen. Follow one appointment into a call and pull back to reveal the owner's dashboard.
strengths: A striking opening with one clear focal point.
Makes the phone feel tangible while the product story stays simple.
The restrained composition gives the headline room to breathe.
concepts.tradeoff: The opening could resemble a phone advertisement. The booking screen must appear early so the service becomes clear.

storyboard.label: 01 / The object
storyboard.visual: A contemporary smartphone stands on a pale stone plinth. Grazing light reveals the stone texture; a small appointment card glows on the screen.

storyboard.label: 02 / The booking
storyboard.visual: The camera approaches the screen as a customer selects a time. The completed appointment card lifts slightly above the glass, remaining the focal point.

storyboard.label: 03 / The confirmation call
storyboard.visual: The same appointment card becomes a restrained outbound call display. A waveform moves beside the customer's appointment details; the phone remains visible behind it.
storyboard.copy: AI calls to confirm the details.

storyboard.label: 04 / The record
storyboard.visual: The waveform settles into a call record with its outcome and transcript. The camera pulls back as the record finds its place in the owner's dashboard.
storyboard.copy: You see how the call went.

concepts.name: A business in miniature
concepts.headline: Keep your business moving.
concepts.subcopy: Give customers a simple way to book online, follow up with an AI confirmation call, and keep the call record close at hand.
concepts.cameraMotion: Orbit a nearly closed miniature creative studio. Slide its front wall aside, move inside toward the booking card and outgoing call, then pull back to reveal the whole studio beside the owner's dashboard.
strengths: Connects the service to the owner's working day.
Creates a memorable world with warmth and depth.
One continuous setting helps explain who benefits at each step.
concepts.tradeoff: A detailed scene can compete with the message. Use one studio without people, minimal props and a clear focus on the booking and outgoing call.

storyboard.label: 01 / Business as usual
storyboard.visual: A miniature boutique creative studio sits inside a nearly closed architectural shell. Warm light escapes through the entrance; there are no people.

storyboard.label: 02 / A new appointment
storyboard.visual: The studio's front wall slides aside to reveal a simple desk and an appointment card. The booking becomes the clear focal point inside the model.

storyboard.label: 03 / A call goes out
storyboard.visual: The camera moves into the studio toward an ordinary smartphone. An outgoing call display and restrained waveform connect the call to the appointment.
storyboard.copy: AI follows up with a confirmation call.

storyboard.label: 04 / Back to the owner
storyboard.visual: The camera pulls back to show the entire open studio. The owner's dashboard appears beside it, displaying the appointment and the completed call record.
storyboard.copy: The call details are there when you need them.

concepts.name: Inside the booking
concepts.headline: One booking. The whole story.
concepts.subcopy: Follow each online booking through its AI confirmation call, with the appointment and call record visible in your dashboard.
concepts.cameraMotion: Start above one appointment card and tilt into a shallow three-dimensional view. Separate four layers for booking, call, transcript and summary, move between them toward the outgoing waveform, then assemble the owner's dashboard.
strengths: Explains the actual product with very little translation.
Makes the transition from booking to call record easy to follow.
Offers clear pauses for readable text and real interface details.
concepts.tradeoff: It may feel like a familiar software demonstration. Strong lighting, depth and carefully timed movement must provide the visual distinction.

storyboard.label: 01 / One appointment
storyboard.visual: A single booking card floats on a quiet background. A selected time and customer name provide a simple, recognizable starting point.
storyboard.copy: It starts with an online booking.

storyboard.label: 02 / The layers
storyboard.visual: The appointment card opens into four distinct layers: booking, call, transcript and summary. Generous space and fine connecting lines reveal how the pieces belong together.
storyboard.copy: Booking, call and details. All connected.

storyboard.label: 03 / The confirmation call
storyboard.visual: The camera moves between the separated layers to feature an outgoing call waveform. The appointment details remain visible nearby, grounding the call in the original booking.
storyboard.copy: AI calls your customer to confirm.

storyboard.label: 04 / The whole picture
storyboard.visual: The layers glide together into the owner's dashboard. A sample confirmed appointment sits beside its call record; the camera returns to a straight-on, readable view.
storyboard.copy: Keep the appointment and call record together.

concepts.name: The next chapter of the phone
concepts.headline: The phone evolved. Your follow-up is next.
concepts.subcopy: From dialling numbers to following up on bookings. Customers book online, AI calls to confirm, and you get the call record.
concepts.cameraMotion: Hold a consistent three-quarter view as a rotary phone becomes a push-button phone, then a smartphone. Give the historic phone sequence the first 45% of the proposed motion; use the final 55% for online booking, the outbound AI confirmation call and the owner's dashboard.
strengths: Creates an immediately recognizable story of change.
Provides three memorable transformations before the product reveal.
Can make the final workflow feel like a natural next step.
concepts.tradeoff: The historical sequence delays the product explanation and could imply AI answers every incoming call. Keep it brief and make the final outbound booking flow explicit.

storyboard.label: 01 / Rotary
storyboard.visual: A sculptural rotary phone sits alone on a simple pedestal. The dial turns slightly as the camera settles into the angle that will remain consistent through the next transformations.

storyboard.label: 02 / Push-button
storyboard.visual: The rotary dial contracts into a push-button keypad. The handset and base reshape into a familiar desk phone while the pedestal, lighting and framing stay continuous.

storyboard.label: 03 / Smartphone
storyboard.visual: The desk phone becomes a slim smartphone. Its screen wakes to an online booking page, bringing the historical sequence into the present product story.
storyboard.copy: Then, we could book from anywhere.

storyboard.label: 04 / The booking gets a call
storyboard.visual: Within one final scene, a submitted booking becomes an outbound AI confirmation call. The completed call record moves into the owner's dashboard as the camera pulls back.
storyboard.copy: Now, AI follows up. You see the result.
